purpose: measurement of the extraction-memo (position-keyed win/loss table) capacity effect and of band-wide cross-root memo sharing on certificate extraction cost for the published cost-73k WIN7-D10 band; no new verdicts, no certificate bytes changed

extractor_engine.memo_spec: MS=1<<18 slots, 64-probe linear probing, memoEntry silently skips on chain exhaustion

precedent_73j.note: same-day 73j band capacity measurement: fresh ms24 -44.7%, band-wide ms24 +2.24% vs fresh (sharing non-contributory); this 73k entry replicates the capacity effect on the 22-bit band and adds memo occupancy instrumentation, the ms22 intermediate point, and a per-root sharing penalty table

sharing_decomposition_same_capacity_ms23.note: band-wide sharing at MS=1<<23 (final load factor 0.8516) is HARMFUL: +11.69% vs fresh per-bit at the same capacity.  Per-bit penalties grow with bit position (open-addressing cluster pollution); only bits 39/41 profit (0.9651/0.9466); bit 95 is memo-state-invariant (1.0000 in every configuration)

fresh_per_bit_ms24.bit112_capacity_monotonicity_note: Fresh per-bit capacity response for bit112 is monotone: ms23=4,767,520 > ms24=4,620,105 nodes (fresh occupancy 934,822/8,388,608 and 1,060,331/16,777,216, far from saturation). An earlier working note recorded an apparent inversion (ms23 4,767,520 < 'ms24' 5,055,110); that 5,055,110 figure is the BAND-WIDE ms24 run's bit112 (shared memo, accumulated occupancy 10,548,738 at that point in the battery), not a fresh per-bit run. The inversion was a band-vs-fresh comparison artifact of the already-documented shared-memo pollution, not hash-mask sensitivity; no capacity-monotonicity violation exists in the fresh data.

band24_sharing_vs_fresh24_same_capacity.note: At ms24 (16,777,216 slots, final load 64.4%) the band-wide sharing penalty collapses to +1.66% versus fresh per-bit tables, compared with +11.69% at ms23 (final load 85.2%). Per-bit ratios span 0.845 (bit41) to 1.159 (bit117): bits 39,41,44,58,73,97 run FASTER under sharing (cross-bit memo reuse) while late-battery bits (89,94,112,117) accumulate pollution as load grows. Sharing harm is load-dependent, not intrinsic: a single shared table at <=~65% load is within ~2% of 22 fresh tables for this workload, which favors one shared memo table per worker over per-root tables at this capacity.

interpretation_guard.certificate_bytes: unchanged (22/22 byte-identical in every completed configuration)
